marks.gloss_en: ששה נחלקין עד עשרה; אי אמרת בשלמא נברך עדיף, משום הכי נחלקין, אלא אי אמרת ברכו עדיף, אמאי נחלקין? אלא לאו שמע מינה נברך עדיף. שמע מינה (50a.2)
but in any case 'let us bless' is preferable
תניא נמי הכי: ...והנקדנין תופסין אותו על כך (that the punctilious reprove 'ברכו' is Steinsaltz's reading of על כך)
whether he said 'bless' or 'let us bless', one does not reprove him for it; and the punctilious reprove him for it
כדתנן: כענין שהוא מברך כך עונין אחריו ברוך ה' אלהי ישראל... -- with ten the Name makes plain to Whom the blessing is addressed
Rav Huna breih deRav Yehoshua: we said this only with three, where there is no Name of Heaven; but with ten, where there is the Name of Heaven, the matter is evident
והכתיב ומברכתך יבורך -- David himself said 'from Your blessing'
בשאלה שאני -- a request is different (= p_bisheela_shani)
בשאלה נמי, הכתיב הרחב פיך ואמלאהו -- in request too, one asks for the full measure
ההוא בדברי תורה כתיב -- that verse is written of words of Torah (= p_harchev_picha_divrei_torah)
but it is written: 'and from Your blessing may Your servant's house be blessed forever' (II Sam 7:29)
והא אמרינן למי שעשה לאבותינו ולנו את כל הנסים האלו -- we ourselves say 'to Him Who'
התם מוכחא מילתא, מאן עביד ניסי -- קודשא בריך הוא: there the matter is evident, for who works miracles? the Holy One
but we say: 'to Him Who performed for our fathers and for us all these miracles'
ולית הלכתא כנהרבלאי -- the halakha is not as Neharbela's reversed version
[one who says] 'by His goodness we live' -- he is a Torah scholar
R' Yochanan: 'let us bless [Him] of Whose we have eaten' -- he is a Torah scholar
R' Yochanan: 'blessed be [He] of Whose we have eaten' -- he is a Torah scholar
דתנן: רבי יוסי הגלילי אומר לפי רוב הקהל הם מברכין -- the graded formulae are his view
אמר רבי עקיבא: מה מצינו בבית הכנסת וכו׳ -- one formula for many or few is his view
לא קשיא: הא רבי יוסי הגלילי, הא רבי עקיבא -- the two clauses are two tannaim (= p_ha_r_yosei_hagelili, p_ha_r_akiva)
Rav Yosef: this [the graded formulae] is R' Yosei HaGelili
הא גופא קשיא: אמרת אחד עשרה ואחד עשרה רבוא, אלמא כי הדדי נינהו, והדר קתני במאה אומר, באלף אומר, ברבוא אומר -- the mishnah contradicts itself
the mishnah: three who ate as one are not permitted to divide
Shmuel: three who sat down to eat as one, and have not yet eaten, are not permitted to divide
Shmuel (second version): this is what it teaches -- three who sat down to eat as one, even though each eats from his own loaf, are not permitted to divide
Rav Chisda: and that is where they came from three companies of three people
Rafram bar Pappa rose, read in the scroll and said 'bless the Lord', and was silent, and did not say 'the blessed One'
two companies that were eating in one house: when some of them see each other, they combine for zimmun
one does not bless over wine until he puts water into it -- the words of R' Eliezer
לא צריכת, הכי אמר רבא: הלכה כרבי עקיבא -- you need not, for thus said Rava: the halakha follows R' Akiva
Rava: the halakha follows R' Akiva
לפי שאין זימון למפרע -- because there is no retroactive zimmun
Rabba Tosefa'a: three who broke bread together, and one of them went ahead and blessed on his own -- they discharge [their obligation] with his zimmun
ואידך? -- and the other [R' Yosei HaGelili], [whence the fetuses' song, if the verse goes to the assembly]?
מ״ממקור״ נפקא -- he derives it from 'from the source' (= p_ryhg_mimekor)
R' Meir: whence that even fetuses in their mothers' wombs sang the song at the Sea? as it is said: 'in assemblies bless God, the Lord, from the source of Israel'
וליברכו עשרה עשרה! -- let them bless in [groups of] ten
שמע ריש גלותא ואיקפד -- the Exilarch would hear and be angry
וניפקו בברכתא דריש גלותא! -- let them discharge [the obligation] with the Exilarch's blessing
איידי דאוושו כולי עלמא, לא שמעי -- since everyone is making noise, they do not hear
Rava: when we eat bread at the Exilarch's, we bless in [groups of] three
